sections.title: Thermoplastic Polyolefin (TPO) Roofing
sections.summary: Thermoplastic Polyolefin (TPO) is a single-ply, heat-weldable thermoplastic membrane. Its standard material performance is governed by ASTM, focusing on weathering, thickness over scrim, and physical aging properties.

entries.claim: TPO membranes must conform to ASTM D6878, establishing minimum properties for thickness, tensile strength, and heat aging.
entries.publication: ASTM D6878: Standard Specification for Thermoplastic Polyolefin Based Sheet Roofing

entries.claim: TPO must have a minimum overall thickness of 45 mils and a minimum thickness-over-scrim of 16 mils.
entries.publication: ASTM D6878: Standard Specification for Thermoplastic Polyolefin Based Sheet Roofing
entries.verification_flag: Required on site to verify mil-weight via micrometer

entries.claim: Heat aging testing requires exposure at 240°F (116°C) for 32 weeks, followed by a mandrel bend test with zero cracking.
entries.publication: Technical Product Data - Sure-Weld TPO

entries.claim: Mechanically attached single-ply membranes require enhanced perimeter fastening zones dictated by ASCE 7 wind load calculations.
entries.publication: ASCE 7-22: Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures

entries.claim: Induction welding TPO systems (e.g., Rhinobond) requires specific plate distribution patterns based on FM Global wind uplift ratings (e.g., 1-90).
entries.publication: GAF EverGuard TPO Application & Specifications Manual
entries.verification_flag: Requires field calibration and pull tests

entries.claim: TPO welding parameters require a consistent seam width of 1.5 inches when utilizing automated hot-air welders.
entries.publication: Elevate TPO Design & Installation Guide
entries.verification_flag: Verified by daily test cuts and destructive peel testing

entries.claim: CONFLICT / OUTDATED FLAG: Older TPO specifications from the early 2000s allowed 1.25-inch seams; modern standards mandate 1.5-inch to 2-inch widths to account for micro-voids.
entries.publication: Technical Bulletin: TPO Seam Geometry Recommendations
entries.verification_flag: Conflict flag: Cross-reference project spec sheets against old warranties

sections.title: EPDM Roofing
sections.summary: Ethylene Propylene Diene Terpolymer (EPDM) is a thermoset synthetic rubber membrane valued for ozone resistance and low-temperature flexibility.

entries.claim: EPDM membrane materials are governed by ASTM D4637, which regulates Type I (non-reinforced) and Type II (scrim-reinforced) sheets.
entries.publication: ASTM D4637: Standard Specification for EPDM Sheet Used In Single-Ply Roof Membrane

entries.claim: NRCA recommends EPDM seams be executed using a minimum 3-inch wide double-sided self-adhering seam tape rather than liquid adhesives.
entries.publication: The NRCA Roofing Manual: Membrane Roof Systems
entries.verification_flag: Field inspection of seam width required

entries.claim: Non-reinforced EPDM exhibits ozone resistance up to 100 pphm (parts per hundred million) at 104°F (40°C) without physical cracking.
entries.publication: RubberGard EPDM Technical Manual

sections.title: PVC Roofing
sections.summary: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) is a thermoplastic membrane reinforced with polyester or fiberglass, offering inherent resistance to chemicals, grease, and oils.

entries.claim: PVC membranes are certified under ASTM D4434, dividing membranes into Type II (fiberglass), Type III (fabric reinforced), and Type IV (high-strength).
entries.publication: ASTM D4434: Standard Specification for Poly(Vinyl Chloride) Sheet Roofing

entries.claim: Type IV PVC membranes require a minimum breaking strength of 275 lbf compared to only 200 lbf for Type III.
entries.publication: Technical Bulletin: PVC Type III vs. Type IV Standards

entries.claim: Standard PVC utilizes liquid plasticizers which can migrate over time, whereas KEE (Ketone Ethylene Ester) uses solid plasticizers to retain flexibility.
entries.publication: Comparative Analysis of PVC and KEE Membranes

sections.title: Modified Bitumen (Mod-Bit) & BUR Assemblies
sections.summary: These heavy-duty asphaltic options include multi-ply built-up roofs and polymer-modified bitumen membranes.

entries.claim: Fiberglass-reinforced SBS membranes must meet ASTM D6163, while polyester-reinforced sheets must meet ASTM D6164.
entries.publication: What Reinforcement Fabric Is Required for Modified Bitumen?

entries.claim: All physical property evaluations (tensile, elongation, tear) for Mod-Bit must be conducted per ASTM D5147.
entries.publication: ASTM D5147: Standard Test Methods for Coated Glass Fabrics Used in Roofing

entries.claim: APP modified bitumen sheets are specified under ASTM D6222 for heat and UV stability.
entries.publication: GAF Commercial Product Manual: APP Membranes

entries.claim: Asphalt-saturated glass felts (Type IV and Type VI) used in BUR must conform to minimum tensile and physical properties under ASTM D2178.
entries.publication: ASTM D2178/D2178M: Standard Specification for Asphalt Glass Felt Used in Roofing and Waterproofing

entries.claim: Asphalt roll-roofing (glass felt) cap sheets surfaced with mineral granules must comply with physical properties under ASTM D3909.
entries.publication: ASTM D3909/D3909M: Standard Specification for Asphalt Roll Roofing (Glass Felt) Surfaced With Mineral Granules

entries.claim: Asphalt-coated glass-fiber venting base sheets, designed for lateral pressure release over lightweight concrete or existing roofs, must meet ASTM D4897 Type II.
entries.publication: ASTM D4897/D4897M-16: Standard Specification for Asphalt-Coated Glass-Fiber Venting Base Sheet Used in Roofing

entries.claim: Asphalt application temperatures (EVT) must be maintained within +/- 25°F (+/- 14°C) of the target temperature at the point of application.
entries.publication: ASTM D4402: Standard Test Method for Viscosity Determinations of Asphalts Using a Rotational Viscometer

entries.claim: Multi-ply configurations must limit the slope to less than 3 inches per foot unless special strapping methods are engineered to prevent sheet slippage.
entries.publication: JM Built-Up Roofing Systems Technical Manual

sections.title: Built-Up Roofing (BUR)
sections.summary: Standard aggregate and organic felt built-up systems rely on asphalt classifications and surface coverage.

entries.claim: Asphalt-saturated organic felts used in BUR must comply with ASTM D226 Type I or Type II.
entries.publication: ASTM D226: Standard Specification for Asphalt-Saturated Organic Felt

entries.claim: Coal tar pitch used in BUR must comply with ASTM D450, providing high resistance to water ponding.
entries.publication: ASTM D450: Standard Specification for Coal-Tar Pitch Used in Roofing

entries.claim: Aggregate surfacing is critical to provide UV shielding and fire resistance per ASTM D1863.
entries.publication: The NRCA Manual: Steep and Low-Slope BUR Assemblies

sections.title: Metal Roofing
sections.summary: Commercial metal systems consist of standing-seam panels that act structural or decorative.

entries.claim: Metal roof systems must resist wind uplift according to the testing criteria established by UL 580.
entries.publication: UL 580: Standard for Tests for Wind Uplift Resistance of Roof Assemblies

entries.claim: Structural metal panel systems are tested under ASTM E1592 to determine structural performance under static air pressure.
entries.publication: ASTM E1592: Standard Test Method for Structural Performance of Sheet Metal Roof

entries.claim: Galvanized coatings must meet ASTM A653 with a minimum G90 coating designation for corrosion protection.
entries.publication: Metal Roofing Technical Bulletin: Anti-Corrosion Standards

sections.title: Roof Coatings
sections.summary: Fluid-applied silicone, acrylic, or urethane membranes are engineered to restore degraded surfaces.

entries.claim: Liquid-applied silicone coatings must comply with ASTM D6694 for physical properties and weathering resistance.
entries.publication: ASTM D6694: Standard Specification for Liquid-Applied Silicone Coatings

entries.claim: Elastomeric acrylic coatings must meet ASTM D6083 requirements for tensile strength and water resistance.
entries.publication: ASTM D6083: Standard Specification for Liquid-Applied Acrylic Coatings

entries.claim: Roof coatings do not replace a deteriorated roof deck; code requires that the existing substrate is dry and structurally sound before application.
entries.publication: GAF Liquid-Applied Roof Restoration Manual
entries.verification_flag: Infrared moisture scan before coating application

sections.title: Roof Inspections & Diagnostics
sections.summary: Accurate diagnostic and scanning standards verify underlying structural and moisture integrity.

entries.claim: Visual roof inspections should follow ASTM D1079 terms and standard operating procedures for visual assessments.
entries.publication: ASTM D1079: Standard Terminology Relating to Roofing and Waterproofing

entries.claim: Non-destructive moisture detection in roofs via infrared thermography is standardized under ASTM C1153, which requires the scan to be performed at least 1 hour after sunset.
entries.publication: ASTM C1153: Standard Practice for Location of Wet Insulation in Roofing Systems

entries.claim: Electronic Leak Detection (ELD) mapping must follow standard conductive media testing parameters for high or low voltage protocols.
entries.publication: ASTM D7877: Standard Guide for Electronic Methods for Detecting Leaks in Waterproof Membranes

entries.claim: NRCA recommends commercial roofs be inspected twice annually (spring and autumn) plus after any major storm event.
entries.publication: NRCA Commercial Roof Maintenance Manual

sections.title: Low-Slope Insulation & Cover Boards
sections.summary: Physical and thermal properties (R-value and compressive strength) determine performance under structural loads and hail impacts.

entries.claim: Polyisocyanurate (Polyiso) insulation boards must conform to the physical testing specifications of ASTM C1289.
entries.publication: ASTM C1289: Standard Specification for Faced Rigid Cellular Polyisocyanurate Thermal Insulation Board
entries.verification_flag: Long-Term Thermal Resistance (LTTR) design value review

entries.claim: High-density gypsum cover boards (e.g., DensDeck, Securock) are required to achieve FM Global Class 1 severe hail (SH) ratings.
entries.publication: FM Property Loss Prevention Data Sheet 1-29: Roof Deck Design

entries.claim: Polyiso exhibits a thermal performance drop (thermal drift) at lower ambient temperatures, which must be accounted for in cold climates.
entries.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
entries.publication: NIST Technical Note 1982: Low-Temperature Thermal Resistance Modeling

sections.title: High-Velocity Hurricane Mitigation & Codes
sections.summary: Coastal regions require rigorous engineering, specialized perimeter edge testing, and mechanical fastening patterns.

entries.claim: Wind design and uplift requirements for insurance and property loss mitigation must be calculated using regional basic wind speeds per FM Global Data Sheet 1-28.
entries.publication: FM Property Loss Prevention Data Sheet 1-28: Wind Design
entries.verification_flag: Compare wind speed design maps against site-specific FM criteria

entries.claim: Roofing projects funded by FEMA grants must comply with FEMA P-804 wind retrofit mitigation guides for high-wind zones.
entries.publication: FEMA P-804: Wind Retrofit Guide for Residential and Low-Rise Buildings

entries.claim: Florida Building Code requires low-slope systems to provide a minimum safety factor of 2.0 over calculated design wind pressures when using laboratory testing values.
entries.publication: 2023 Florida Building Code, Fifth Edition - Chapter 15

entries.claim: FEMA recommends upgrading perimeter fastener spacing by a factor of 50% relative to standard field density inside high-wind risk bands.
entries.publication: FEMA P-424: Design Guide for Improving School Safety in Earthquakes, Floods, and High Winds

entries.claim: Edge metal configurations must be certified under ANSI/SPRI ES-1 to resist high wind stress on commercial properties.
entries.publication: ANSI/SPRI ES-1: Wind Design Standard for Edge Systems Used with Low Slope Roofing Systems

sections.title: Roof Life Expectancy
sections.summary: Service lifespan is modeled using thermal loading, material composition, and long-term degradation curves.

entries.claim: Typical service life for EPDM is 25-30 years, TPO is 20-25 years, and PVC is 20-25 years if properly installed.
entries.publication: PNNL Study on Low-Slope Roof Lifespans

entries.claim: BUR life expectancy averages 20-30 years, but drops sharply without adequate UV aggregate cover.
entries.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
entries.publication: NIST IR 6231: Service Life of Low-Slope Roofs

entries.claim: Double-ply Mod-Bit assemblies can yield a service life of 20-25 years under standard environmental exposure.
entries.publication: GAF Commercial Low-Slope Application Manual

sections.title: Commercial Roof Maintenance & Safety
sections.summary: Maintenance guidelines maintain warranty compliance and follow federal fall protection standards.

entries.claim: OSHA standard 1910.28 requires fall protection for any personnel performing roof maintenance on a roof with unprotected sides or edges 4 feet or more above a lower level.
entries.publication: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.28: Duty to Have Fall Protection

entries.claim: For preventive maintenance, OSHA 1910.28 organizes rooftop protection by distance from the edge: workers between 6 and 15 feet from the edge must be protected by a guardrail, safety net, travel restraint, or personal fall arrest system.
entries.publication: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.28: Duty to Have Fall Protection

entries.claim: FM Global requires commercial drains to be cleared of debris to prevent structural overloading from ponding water.
entries.publication: FM Property Loss Prevention Data Sheets 1-54: Roof Systems

entries.claim: Maintaining historical repair logs is a universal requirement to avoid denial of commercial system warranties.
entries.publication: The NRCA Guidelines for Commercial Roof Maintenance

sections.title: Insurance Claims
sections.summary: Insurance requirements demand clear historical documentation and compliance with local statutory codes.

entries.claim: Florida's '25 Percent Rule' requires that if more than 25% of a roof section is damaged within 12 months, the entire section must be brought to current building code.
entries.publication: Florida Building Code - Existing Building (Section 706.1.1 / Section 1512)

entries.claim: Post-disaster roof structural reviews must be documented by a licensed professional engineer to confirm wind uplift structural failure.
entries.publication: FEMA Mitigation Assessment Team (MAT) Reports

entries.claim: Pre-existing unmitigated roof damage is the leading cause of denied commercial property insurance claims.
entries.publication: Commercial Property Insurance Claim Audits

sections.title: Repair vs. Replacement
sections.summary: Determining the transition point between restoration and full replacement is governed by code-mandated moisture percentages and layering limits.

entries.claim: If moisture scans show more than 25% of the insulation is saturated, a full replacement is recommended over a restoration coating.
entries.publication: NRCA Low-Slope Roof Restoration Manual

entries.claim: The International Building Code (IBC) limits low-slope roofs to a maximum of two roofing system layers before complete tear-off is required.
entries.publication: 2024 International Building Code (IBC), Section 1512.3: Roof Recover

entries.claim: Structural dead weight calculations must be completed when adding a second layer to ensure the structure can support the new dead load.
entries.publication: International Building Code (IBC), Chapter 16: Structural Loads

sections.title: White Roof vs. Black Roof (Cool Roofs)
sections.summary: Cool roof metrics use solar reflectance index values to calculate performance across climatic zones.

entries.claim: Cool roofs must have a high Solar Reflectance Index (SRI), calculated using equations in ASTM E1980.
entries.publication: ASTM E1980: Standard Practice for Calculating Solar Reflectance Index

entries.claim: In ASHRAE Climate Zones 1-3 (Southern US), white roofs can reduce roof surface temperatures by up to 50°F (28°C), lowering peak HVAC loads.
entries.publication: DOE Cool Roof Installation and Energy Studies

entries.claim: In ASHRAE Climate Zones 5-8 (Northern US), cool roofs can cause a heating penalty where the building requires more heating fuel in winter.
entries.publication: LBNL Cool Roof Heat Load Interdependency Report
